tasks.current_review_risk: Non-rolling wheel, unsqueezed tube and estimated force weaken defining mechanics.
tasks.validation_scope: Existing published simulation repeatability, adversarial scorer behavior and retained media; NOT real IV flow shutoff, clinical force validation, construct validity approval or prediction of acceptance.

validation_limits: Wheel is prismatic only: a ribbed disc slides and cannot rotate; tubing is not squeezed. The defining rolling/compression mechanics and actual no-flow endpoint are absent. Published fidelity discloses this; disclosure alone does not establish construct validity.

Wheel3N and carrier1.5N friction are estimates selected to make unsupported push slide before wheel advances. Simulated breakaway measurements characterize this implemented model, not the physical IV clamp. A source-supported approximate force law and sensitivity test may suffice under accepted precedents; exact OEM CAD or own hardware measurement is not a blanket prerequisite.

40mm whole-run slide disqualification and 15mm remaining-slack threshold are bench proxies without demonstrated cannula force/dislodgement correspondence. Sliding an otherwise slack closed clamp need not be clinical harm. This can manufacture difficulty and penalize legitimate strategies.
README real success additionally requires no drip for30s; simulation/full metadata only require wheel position. 60%travel partial credit has no established flow/safety equivalence.

Named BD set264cm differs from the documented total local tube sections around151.6cm including clamp; shortening/custom setup should be explicit. Modeled clamp dimensions are estimates and exact compatible hardware is not established.

Occupational nursing relevance is plausible, but single wheel push may be judged too minor or generic; whole occupation employment is not operation frequency. No probability of acceptance assigned here.

The high downward command (16mm nominal overlap converted through native arm compliance) succeeds in sim but is not force-measured against real tubing/clamp damage. Native tactile/contact force evidence and sensible parameter sensitivity remain useful.
tasks.note: Historical controls and diagnostic cleanup recovered exactly; no extra GPU runs. Main successful demo is legitimately one-arm; careless one-arm control scores zero. Pending PR unchanged.
tasks.acceptance_reason: Real-world trials would be too difficult to reproduce consistently; review also says importance bar not met, not revisable.
